detailed_description: TSConfig Generator helps you create customized TypeScript configuration files for your projects. Configure compiler options including target ECMAScript version, module system, strict mode settings, and path aliases. Choose from presets for React, Node.js, library development, or create a custom configuration. The tool explains each option and generates a complete tsconfig.json file with comments explaining the settings. TSConfig Generator is intended for quick drafting, checking, and review of developer-facing inputs rather than unattended automation. Use the result as a starting point, inspect assumptions or formatting details in the interface, and verify important code, configuration, or deployment changes before you publish or deploy them.
usage_steps: Select a project type preset (React, Node.js, Library, etc.)
Enable strict mode options as needed
Set up path aliases for imports
Configure output directory and other options
Click Generate and copy the tsconfig.json
usage_examples: Set up TypeScript for a new React project
Configure TypeScript for a Node.js backend
Create a tsconfig for a npm package library
Set up path aliases for cleaner imports

faqs.question: What should I check before using the TSConfig Generator output?
faqs.answer: Review code, configuration, parsing details, and any assumptions before using the result in a repository, script, or deployment workflow.

faqs.question: Can I edit the result after generating it?
faqs.answer: Yes. Adjust the input values or available options, generate the result again, and then copy, export, or reuse the updated output in your workflow when the page provides those actions.

faqs.question: Why might the result differ from another development tool?
faqs.answer: Different tools can use different assumptions, rounding rules, parsing behavior, or export settings. Compare the same input values and review any notes shown in the interface before relying on the result.

faqs.question: Can I start with sample or placeholder data?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use a small example or non-sensitive sample first, confirm the output shape, and then replace it with the real input you want to process.

faqs.question: Does this replace manual review?
faqs.answer: No. It can speed up routine work, but generated code, configuration, or diagnostics should still be reviewed and tested.
